title: Undoing Changes: Restore, Reset & Revert
description: Safely discard working tree edits, unstage files, adjust branch pointers with reset, and reverse public commits with revert.

blocks.content: You changed the wrong file before a demo. You need to choose a recovery action that does not erase more work than intended. What is the smallest Git action that keeps the work safe?

Choose the smallest recovery tool that fits. `git restore file` discards an unstaged file change, while `git revert` makes a new commit that reverses a published commit.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Working files"] -->|"choose an action"| B["Git history"] -->|"share or recover"| C["Team project"]
```

blocks.question: A shared commit is wrong. Which action preserves history?
blocks.explanation: A revert adds a visible correction without rewriting shared history.

blocks.prompt: Model the Git idea in a tiny simulator. Export a function named `restoreFile` that takes `(working, staged, file)` and returns a new staged list containing `file` once. Do not change either input list.

tests.description: works when no working files are listed yet
keeps an already staged file while adding another
